## Property overrides on instanced children

`set_node_properties` reported success on a node living inside an instanced child scene and then dropped the change on save. Nodes inside an instanced scene are not owned by the scene root, so `PackedScene.pack()` skipped their overrides entirely, which left the `.tscn` on disk unchanged while the call returned cleanly. Nothing surfaced the loss, and any caller that did not re-read the file to check had no way to know the edit never landed.

The fix is the same "editable children" mechanism the Godot editor uses. Each instanced ancestor is marked editable from the scene root, so the override serializes alongside the `instance=ExtResource(...)` link rather than vanishing. Composing a scene out of instanced children and then adjusting a node inside one now persists, and it stays persisted across repeated writes to the same path.

**This changes what reaches disk, not what the tool reports.** If you have been setting properties on nodes inside instanced children, those calls were succeeding and silently doing nothing. They now take effect.

## set_node_properties inside batch_scene_operations

`batch_scene_operations` accepts `set_node_properties` as a sub-operation. Items take the same per-update params as the standalone tool (`nodePath`, `property`, `value`), plus a per-operation `scenePath` and `abortOnError`, and per-update results come back under `results[].updates`. Both paths run through one shared apply routine, so validation, type checking, and serialization behave identically whether you call the tool directly or batch it with `add_node` and `load_sprite` in a single Godot process.

Thanks to [@mcanevet](https://github.com/mcanevet) for finding and fixing the serialization bug.
